I made an open-source, ad-free content downloader that simply works


Every time I tried downloading a video online, I ended up on some shady website full of popups, fake buttons, and trackers. All I wanted was a clean, safe way to download content for offline viewing, education, and inspiration - without ads or hidden scripts.
So I created Fetchy an open source ad free content downloader which is fast, privacy-friendly and operates directly from your browser.
I grew tired of fake “Download” links, annoying redirect loops and websites that use your bandwidth to display ads.
Fetchy was created on a premise that transparent and user respectful utilities should be open demoninator.
🚫 No ads or tracking - first and foremost, privacy.
Open source - inspect, fork, or contribute to it on GitHub.
Just works - clean interface, no extensions or sign up needed.
Modern solutions - lightweight front-end and moderate back-end that doesn't bag down on popular sites.
🌐 Try it
fetchy.app
github.com
If you find it useful, or just plain interesting, then a ⭐ on GitHub means the world.
And if you have thoughts on making it better, open an issue or get in the discussion - I’d love to collaborate with the community.

articles.author: Mohamed Ahmed
articles.description:
Introduction


Hello, world! 👋 I'm starting this blog to document my journey into the Internet of Things (IoT) using the powerful and popular ESP32 microcontroller. Whether you're a hobbyist, a student, or just curious, I invite you to follow along. We'll start from the absolute beginning, and our first mission is to get our development environment up and running. By the end of this post, you will have the Arduino IDE installed and configured for your ESP32 board.
A computer (Windows, Mac, or Linux)
An ESP32 development board (like the ESP32 DevKit C)
A USB cable (typically Micro-USB or USB-C, depending on your board)
STEP 1: Installing the Arduino IDE


The Arduino IDE (Integrated Development Environment) is where we will write our code, compile it, and upload it to the ESP32.
Download the IDE: Go to the official Arduino Software page. Avoid the "Web Editor" for now; we want the IDE. Download the version for your operating system.
Run the Installer:
Windows: Run the downloaded .exe file. It's recommended to let it install the necessary drivers.
Mac: Drag the Arduino IDE application into your Applications folder.
Linux: Extract the folder and run the install.sh script.
Open the Arduino IDE: Once installed, open the application. You should see a clean, mostly empty window. This is your coding canvas!
articles.title: Welcome to the World of IoT: Your First Steps with Arduino IDE and ESP32

articles.author: Denis Sirashev
articles.description:
The problem


While working on my NodeJS project, I encountered issues with large Docker images while building them from the source code. The problem was that Docker copied all files, including the node_modules folder, despite having a line in .dockerignore that excluded' node_modules'.
node_modules

Why didn't it work properly? It was a monorepo PNPM project, and ignoring the node_modules folder with a simple node_modules was not enough. The key was that the context of building images was rooted in the project's foundation. I didn't have node_modules in the project's root, but had it inside each application and package. To solve that, I've added another line in my .dockerignore file:
**/node_modules

So now, it doesn't copy any of the node_modules folders inside applications, packages, and services. Each image has its own node_modules folder during the installation process. Simple and clean.
Photo by Favour Usifo on Unsplash
articles.title: Quick tip 2 - Completely ignore node_modules for Docker in Monorepo
